verses.140:1: Senhor, clamei a vós, escutai-me: * atendei à minha voz, quando eu clamar a vós.
verses.140:4: Não {declines} o meu coração para palavras de malícia, * {excusandas} nos pecados.
verses.140:4b: Com os homens que praticam a iniquidade: * e não {communicabo} com {electis}.
verses.140:5: {corripiet} com misericórdia, e me repreenderá: * mas o óleo do pecador não {impinguet} a minha cabeça.
verses.140:6: Porque ainda a minha oração também está {beneplacitis}: * foram engolidos, {juncti}, os seus juízes.
verses.140:7: Ouvirão as minhas palavras, {potuerunt}: * como {crassitudo} sobre a terra.
verses.140:8: Foram dispersos os nossos ossos junto ao {infernum}: * porque para vós, Senhor, Senhor, estão os meus olhos: em vós esperei, não tireis a minha alma.
verses.140:9: Guardai-me do laço que {statuerunt} para mim: * e dos tropeços dos que praticam a iniquidade.
verses.140:10: Cairão {ejus} os pecadores: * {singulariter} até que eu passe.

decisions.why: The best-known line of the psalm: sung at the incensation of the altar in the traditional Mass (DO Ordo, with Dómine added), as a Gradual, and as the Sunday Vespers versicle, which splits it after orátio mea (circulation.md). Every Brazilian text found says 'suba' (Tridentine hand-missal, CNBB, the lectionary refrain 'Minha oração suba a vós como incenso'), and Matos Soares 1932 has 'Suba direita'. But the Latin verb is dirígere (κατευθυνθήτω, be set straight, be directed), not a verb of rising; and the rising is the second colon's own image (elevátio). 'Suba' would swap the Latin's word for another and anticipate elevátio, so under D2 it is refused and kept as the first option. The dirígere row is 'dirigir', with the passive kept where the Latin has it (118:5 'sejam dirigidos', 118:128). The subject is put first on purpose: 'Seja dirigida a minha oração' is heard as 'dirigida à minha oração' (addressed to my prayer), since a and à sound alike; 'Que' is the jussive head, as 87:3 'Que entre na vossa presença a minha oração'. The versicle split still falls cleanly: 'Que a minha oração seja dirigida. R. Como incenso na vossa presença.' Syllables 22 for the Latin's 21.

decisions.why: The Latin colon has no verb and no 'sicut': the lifting of the hands is set beside the evening sacrifice. It is sung alone as the Gradual verse, so it must stand alone; the verbless apposition does. 'Elevação' keeps eleváre → elevar (glossary, which names 140:2). 'Vespertino' is the Latin's adjective and is everyday Brazilian (the afternoon school shift), and it ties the line to Vespers; the Tridentine hand-missal has 'sacrifício vespertino' (circulation.md). 'Da tarde' (MS1932, CNBB 'oferta da tarde') is plainer by a hair and two syllables shorter.

decisions.why: The custodíre row asks 140:3 to copy the noun of 38:2b 'Pus guarda à minha boca' (Pósui ori meo custódiam), the same Latin words: bare 'guarda', as 'pôr guarda' (to post a guard). The verse is also a responsory and part of the incensation prayer, where Brazilian texts say 'uma guarda' (MS1932, CNBB, hand-missal).

options.label: uma guarda
options.note: MS1932, CNBB, the hand-missal; breaks the echo with 38:2b.

decisions.why: Circumstántia is 'a standing round, a surrounding' (L&S); the Greek θύραν περιοχῆς is a door of enclosure. The cognate 'circunstância' means a circumstance in Portuguese and is refused. The noun becomes a relative clause ('que os cerque'), which is grammar (D2); 'cercar' is to enclose, of the family of 'cerca' (fence), which keeps the image of a surrounding wall. The dative 'lábiis meis' stays a dative ('aos meus lábios'), set chiastically against 'à minha boca'.

decisions.latin: Non declínes cor meum in verba malítiæ
decisions.why: Declináre here is transitive with God as subject: 'do not turn my heart aside to' (ἐκκλίνῃς). 'Inclinar' is what Brazil says (CNBB 'Meu coração não deixeis inclinar-se') but it is inclináre's verb, and 118:36 'Inclína cor meum in testimónia tua' → 'Inclinai o meu coração para os vossos testemunhos' is the same build with the other verb (κλῖνον): by D15's test the two stay two. The declináre row has 'apartar-se de' (with 'a'), 'se desviaram' (absolute) and 'voltar' (20:12, 54:4, evils turned against someone). 'Desviar para' says the turning aside that the prefix de- and ἐκ- carry; its cost is that the row keeps transitive 'desviar' for avértere, which is not in this psalm. Colon +3 syllables over the Latin.

options.label: inclineis
options.note: What Brazilian ears know; merges with inclináre (118:36).

decisions.why: A figura etymologica, verb and noun of one root, as in the Greek (τοῦ προφασίζεσθαι προφάσεις); D2 keeps the Latin's repetitions (cf. 4:6 'Sacrificai um sacrifício'). 'Desculpar-se com desculpas' keeps both halves and is Portuguese; the reflexive infinitive leaves the person open, as the gerundive does. MS1932 and the hand-missal ('buscar desculpas', 'procurando pretextos') drop the verb.

options.label: para dar desculpas
options.note: DRB 'to make excuses'; plain, the repetition lost.

decisions.why: Communicáre cum is 'to share, have fellowship with' (συνδυάσω, to be paired with). The cognate 'comunicar' is to communicate (talk) in Portuguese; 'comungar com' is heard first as receiving Communion. 'Ter comunhão com' keeps the root in the noun and the sense of fellowship. The future is kept (communicábo).

options.label: comungarei
options.note: The root verb; heard as receiving Communion.

decisions.why: Eléctis can be masculine (their chosen men, DRB 'the choicest of them') or neuter (their choice things, their dainties — which is the Hebrew's sense, MS1932 'as suas delícias', not followed). The Greek is as open as the Latin. 'Os escolhidos deles' is the glossary's word (104:43 'os seus escolhidos') and leans to persons, as Portuguese must; 'deles' rather than 'seus' so that it is not heard as the psalmist's or God's.

decisions.latin: Corrípiet me justus … et increpábit me
decisions.why: Both verbs are future indicative (παιδεύσει … ἐλέγξει), not wishes: 'the just man will chastise me in mercy'. MS1932 makes them jussive ('Corrija-me o justo'), the Hebrew's mood; the Latin's is kept. The verbs are the glossary's: corrípere → castigar (D21), increpáre → repreender. The row for corrípere names this verse. 'In misericórdia' → 'com misericórdia', the manner (ἐν ἐλέει).

options.label: Castigue-me o justo
options.note: MS1932's jussive; the second verb would have to become 'e me repreenda'.

decisions.why: The impinguáre row ('Ungistes com óleo a minha cabeça', 22:5b) says 140:5 must follow. The same oil and head: 'não unja a minha cabeça'. 'Untar' keeps the fat and was the row's option; 'engordar' is the Latin's first sense, withdrawn by the 22:5b Latinist himself.

decisions.latin: Quóniam adhuc et orátio mea in beneplácitis eórum
decisions.why: The Latin is obscure and has no verb: 'for still also my prayer [is] in their good pleasures'. DRB and MS1932 read 'in' as 'against' ('against the things with which they are well pleased', 'é contra o que lhe apraz') — that is the Hebrew's sense ('against their evil deeds') carried into the Latin, and it is not what 'in' says. The copula 'está' is supplied (D2) and 'in' kept as 'em'; the noun beneplácitum (row open; 'favor' at 88:18, but the plural 'favores' is 'favours done') becomes the relative 'o que lhes agrada' — grammar, the root of placére → agradar kept. Whether the prayer is set among, about or against what pleases them is left open, as the Latin leaves it. 'Et' → 'também'.

options.label: nos seus agrados
options.note: Keeps a noun; 'agrados' is heard as small gifts or caresses.

options.label: contra o que lhes agrada
options.note: DRB, MS1932: clearer, but it is the Hebrew's sense; refused.

decisions.latin: absórpti sunt juncti petræ júdices eórum
decisions.why: 'Their judges, joined to the rock, were swallowed up' (the Greek ἐχόμενα πέτρας, 'close by the rock'). DRB's 'falling upon the rock' and MS1932's 'precipitados ao longo dos rochedos' explain; the Latin says only 'joined'. absorbére → engolir (row), petra → rocha (row), definite here as a named place in the image. Why they are joined to the rock is left as the Latin leaves it. 'Os seus juízes', since the first colon already has 'lhes'.

options.label: junto à rocha
options.note: The Greek's 'beside'; the participle becomes a preposition.

decisions.why: 'Because they were able / had power' (the Latin read ἠδυνήθησαν; the Rahlfs text prints ἡδύνθησαν 'were sweet'; the Latin is followed). Who had power — the words or the men who will hear them — is open: MS1932 resolves it to the words ('porque elas são poderosas'). Bare 'porque puderam' is not a finished sentence in Portuguese ('because they could … what?'). 'Tiveram poder' keeps the root and the Latin's open subject, since it has no gender.

options.label: porque puderam
options.note: The literal verb; heard as incomplete.

options.label: porque foram poderosas
options.note: MS1932: the words made the subject; resolves the ambiguity.

decisions.latin: sicut crassitúdo terræ erúpta est super terram
decisions.why: Crassitúdo is 'thickness' (L&S; πάχος), not a clod or a crust, which would explain. 'Espessura' is the word. Erúpta est (passive, perfect) → 'se rompeu', the pronominal form for a passive with a thing as subject (grammar); DRB 'is broken up'. The Latin says 'terra' twice (terræ … super terram) and so does the Portuguese; DRB varies it (earth / ground), and that is not followed. The obscurity is the Latin's own; the Hebrew's ploughing is not imported.

decisions.why: The inférnus row is open and heavy (D22); the finished psalms keep 'inferno' (6:6, 15:10, 138:8 'se eu descer ao inferno'). Here 'beside hell' is where the bones lie scattered, which is the abode of the dead; 'inferno' is kept for the row. dissipáre → dispersar for bones strewn (the row's proposal; 52:6b, 21:15).

options.label: abismo
options.note: Avoids the hell of the damned; it is abýssus's word (41:8). Refused.

decisions.why: The statúere row is 'firmar' (118:38, 17:34, 24:12), but 'firmar um laço' is not what one does with a snare. 'Armar um laço' is the Portuguese idiom for setting a trap and says what statúere says here (set up). MS1932 'armaram'. 'Pôr um laço' is pónere's (118:110 'puseram um laço para mim') and would merge two verbs. Cost: 'armar' is also 'inténdere arcum' (armar o arco); they do not meet here. 'Para mim' as 118:110.

options.label: firmaram
options.note: The statúere row; heard as odd for a trap.

decisions.why: Ejus is singular and not reflexive: 'his net', not 'their own net' (which would be suo / eórum). Whose — God's, or an enemy's — the Latin does not say. Portuguese 'na sua rede' would be heard as 'their own net' (MS1932 glosses 'sua (própria)'), a resolution the Latin's grammar excludes; 'dele' keeps singular and open. retiáculum → rede (rete's word; the diminutive is not marked).
The singuláriter row is 'a sós' (4:10). Kept; 'eu' named as the Latin's 'ego' does, and again in 'até que eu passe' so that 'passe' is not heard as 'he passes'. MS1932 'estou só'.

options.label: sozinho estou eu,
options.note: Plainer; a masculine the Latin does not have.

choices.140:1: No titulus: DO's file has none (D7), though the LXX and MS1932 print 'Salmo de David'. clamáre → clamar with the perfect kept ('clamei a vós', as 129:1); exáudi → escutai (D3), inténde → atendei (D3; the glossary lists 140:1 among the four places where the two stand parallel). 'eu' supplied in the second colon so that 'quando clamar' has its subject. The first colon reads alone as the antiphon 'Dómine, clamávi ad te, exáudi me'.
choices.140:2: The verse is said at the incensation and as a Gradual; each colon stands alone. The versicle split (after 'orátio mea') falls after 'seja dirigida'. in conspéctu → 'na vossa presença', the conspéctus row's split for an act of worship (137:1b, 87:3).
choices.140:4: The Latin's two cola run on into 140:4b ('Cum homínibus …'), so 140:4 ends with a comma as the Latin does.
choices.140:4b: operári iniquitátem → 'praticar a iniquidade' (glossary). 'os homens' with the article: 'com homens que praticam' would be heard as 'together with such men' only; the article keeps the class.
choices.140:6: absorbére → engolir (row open; 123:3b's 'tragado' was a local departure where two verbs stood together).
choices.140:8: The verse has one asterisk and an inner colon; the colon is kept as punctuation. 'Dómine, Dómine' repeated as the Latin. The copula 'estão' supplied (D2). auferre → tirar (D41). quia → porque (the default).
choices.140:9: scándalum → tropeço (row; 139:6 has the same word); custódi me → Guardai-me (custodíre row).

audit.note: Draft 1 from the parallels. Liturgical use and Brazilian circulation fetched into circulation.md: every Brazilian text found has 'suba' for Dirigátur; refused for the Latin's verb (decision dirigatur). Hard readings: 140:6 (in beneplácitis, juncti petræ), 140:7 (potuérunt, crassitúdo), all left as obscure as the Latin is; the Hebrew's senses (DRB and MS1932's 'contra', 'precipitados', 'delícias') not imported.

Hard checks pass. Soft length flags accepted: 140:2 first colon +3 by the counter (Que‿a and minha‿oração elide in the mouth: about +1 said; the subject is first to avoid the a/à mishearing, decision dirigatur); 140:2 second colon -3 (verbless, as the Latin); 140:4 first colon +4 (Portuguese needs the article and 'para'; 'desvieis' four syllables for 'declínes' three); 140:6 second colon +3 (the participle and the article); 140:8 first colon +3 ('junto ao' for 'secus'). No cadence faults; no accidental rhyme at mediant and final.
